title: A prop sunk a few mm into a slab reads as 'floating 56-125 cm'
summary: The contact ray starts inside a slab and hits its underside: a chip sunk 7 mm (or a tilted tower base) reads 'floating' by the slab's thickness. Rest props on the surface + 1 mm.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

doc.when: Rocks, chips, debris, tilted objects on slabs or thin ground boxes.
doc.avoid: Embedding props 'a bit' to hide gaps; tilting about the centre (one edge sinks).
gotchas: Pivot a tilt on the edge that stays on the surface.
Engine fix wanted: rays from the top of the box, or treat inside as touching.

problem.symptom: FLOATING 56 cm (chip) or 92-125 cm (tower) for something visibly sitting on the ground.
problem.cause: The ray starts inside the slab and the hit is the slab's underside; the distance is the slab thickness.
problem.fix: Place the prop's lowest point 1 mm above the surface; pivot tilts on a ground edge.
problem.detect: The reported float equals a slab's thickness.
